pairs.subject: keyboard-shortcuts
pairs.evidence: apps/console/src/keys/listener.ts:40 The console's only keydown listener checks just defaultPrevented and modifier-only keys. It never looks at e.repeat or e.isComposing, so holding Enter in the review player runs the non-idempotent 'Save and next' over and over, and keys an input method is composing reach the resolver.

techniques.evidence: apps/console/src/keys/keymap.ts:83 There is one plain-data table of chord, modes, action, label and scope. The listener resolves through it, and conflictReport runs as a test. Readers outside this context (Player.tsx kbd hints, Chrome.tsx aria-keyshortcuts) restate keys by hand, and no reference page renders the labels. See notes.

apps/console/src/keys/keymap.ts:151 One dispatch point resolves the innermost data-key-scope first and the global bindings second. An unowned binding does not resolve, so it is never prevented. Shell.tsx reads handler context through a ref, so the listener is installed once. Widgets that handle a key preventDefault it, and the listener skips those events.

apps/console/src/keys/keymap.ts:126 The listener has no repeat filter, no composition skip and no check that the key is a string. A keydown with no key, such as an autofill event, throws inside the window listener. Bindings have no repeatable flag, so every action repeats while its key is held.

apps/console/src/keys/keymap.ts:95 The typing guard exists (isTypingTarget). But the bare letters m and r and the bare digits 1-9 are screen-wide accelerators with no off switch, no remap and no focus scoping, which the character-key criterion forbids. A focused type-ahead composite also takes these keys.
